utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we hear the witness. I believe that tomorrow afternoon we'll start at 4.30 instead of 2.15 since this courtroom will be occupied by another hearing. And we understand that we have a very tight schedule, and there are so many witnesses on the list for this week, so we try to find some other time to make up the time we lost tomorrow afternoon, which means we might have four sittings a day some day. Yes, are there any other matters perhaps that you would like to raise? Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is one other matter that I would like to raise, and that is we now would like to make an application to withdraw one witness which was due to come to give his testimony tomorrow, and the name of that witness is Vlajcic, Gusto. And I have -- I had proofed this witness this morning, Your Honour, and I have given over to the Defence the proofing notes and I also alerted them by telephone that we will be making such an application. They do have the proofing notes, and I'll give the following reasons as to why we wish to withdraw him. Firstly, Your Honour, the witness invited me not to lead certain testimony, and that was about the Muslim soldiers and the church. As he said, it would beg the question from the Defence as to why the soldiers did not shoot at him, as he was an HVO officer in uniform, given that he had stated in his statement and he wished to say in court that the ABiH wanted to kill all Croats. He thought that this might be inconsistent and I should leave this aspect of his testimony out entirely. He stated to me that the Defence might pressure him for the truth. Your Honour, in respect of another aspect of his testimony, and that is what he heard about the intercepted communications of the ABiH, as he was a communication commander, he said he heard over the radio, because the ABiH had actually taken over the communication of the ABiH [sic]: Retreat, the enforcements are coming. This was something he had not mentioned before. And he also stated that he does not remember the name "Sefer" in what he had -- what was reflected in his 2000 statement which said: "Act according to Sefer's order." He said to me that he had not heard the name Sefer Halilovic prior to this time and he is not sure how it came to be attributed to him. He also then said to me that Nikolai probably misunderstood him and: "I can't remember whether I mentioned the name Sefer." He further stated to me, and he said: "I thought if I mentioned the name Sefer it would be a problem for me. I could bring myself into an uncomfortable position with this one word, and I could deny everything I said in my statement. The name is not important, but the important thing is that the crimes were done. Your Honour, he further stated to me that there -- that Nikolai behaved like an amateur when recording his statement and he was not a professional. Your Honour, when I advised the witness that it appears to me that he might not be in a position to assist the Trial Chamber with his testimony and that I will not call him, he stated that he really wants to testify before this Chamber. And, If you want, he said, I will not only say Sefer's first name but will also say "Halilovic," and that is -- the name that he heard in that intercepted communication. Because now he's a hundred per cent sure he heard his full name being mentioned by the ABiH soldiers. Your Honours, the Prosecution does not feel that this is a credible witness, and therefore would now respectfully make this application to have him withdrawn from the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any response from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecutor advised us of this matter before giving us the proofing notes. We were told of this -- I can't remember how many minutes ago it was, but quite recently. But on the information provided in this Court, the Prosecutor would have no choice but to make the application that she makes. The Defence does not oppose it. It seems to me it would simply be inevitable in that situation that the Prosecution would behave. I express my gratitude to the learned Prosecutor for advising us as soon as she could. The proofing notes only came at the very end, but I want to place on the record, because we've been critical on other occasions, we want to place on the record here that we were advised orally sometime before that, and I take it rather as the situation developed. In those circumstances it's a matter for the Court to decide, but we think the Prosecutor has got no choice but to act as she has, and we'd make no further comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since the matter how to present their case is entirely in the hands of the party who is calling the witness and taking into consideration of the reasonings presented by the Prosecution, this Bench granted the request from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we are not going to hear that witness. Yes, anything else? Well, so could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I've been just informed by the Court Deputy that there's a possibility for us to sit on Friday starting from 10.30 in the morning until 12.00, then we make a break and continue our sitting at 2.15 until 7.00. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday in your evidence we had got as far as the morning of the 14th of September, 1993, when you heard shooting outside which was coming close and you went outside with your Kalashnikov. It was light and you stayed outside for several minutes and your mother remained inside. Just to go back on that briefly from yesterday, when you went outside did you see -- I asked you yesterday: "Did you see who was shooting?" And you said: "Not at that time, I just saw the direction from which the bullets were flying in." Now, when you went outside that first time, did you see any people with guns?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you fire your own weapon when you went outside the first time?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you stayed outside for a few moments and then you went back inside. What did you do when you went back inside?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told my mother to get ready, that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did your mother do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She stood up and she started to pack while I went back outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you take your weapon with you when you went back outside?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry. Was the shooting continuing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It increased in intensity and then at one point I decided to fire back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go when you went outside a second time?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went as far as the corner of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you decided to shoot back. Did you in fact shoot back?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you fire?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you fire?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the shots were coming from, all sorts of unusual places in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please just clarify that. You said "all sorts of unusual places." Are you saying that you shot in all sorts of unusual places or the fire was coming from all sorts of unusual places?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just one place the shots were coming from, from the woods, and the bullets flew in the direction of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you fire in that direction?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fired several shots, not the whole magazine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you fire?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought at the time that I was able to return fire, but I soon gave up. There was far too much fire coming my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there response to your firing into the woods?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the response like?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a response by automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the door of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you consider yourself to be covered from the position in which you were in when you fired towards the woods?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't consider myself covered. It was still too dangerous. And that's why I decided to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go into the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took my mother as far as the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your mother dressed at that point?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you and your mother do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told her not to leave the house without me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know someone called Ivan Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How old was --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that person quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How old was he in 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 14 or 15. I think he was born back in 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did he live relative to your house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a neighbouring house, very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see him when you went outside on either of those occasions, that's the first two times you went outside when there was firing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he and what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at the window of his house facing my door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he doing at the window?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me, What's going on?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something was wrong, it was too close, and he would be better off running for his life.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He disappeared from the window and I have no idea where he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just go back to when you went into the house with your mother. You told her not to leave the house without you. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked in the direction of the road junction in my village to see what exactly was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Go on. Where were your mother when you looked in the direction of the road junction?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was right behind me near the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you see when you looked out -- when you looked out into the village in the direction of the road junction?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing up to that point. There was a great deal of shooting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you and your mother leave the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do at that time? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did when you looked out the window at the -- down towards the junction, the road junction, your mother is in the house, you're at the door looking out. What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't much of a view from the door. I had to look over the wall. I looked at my mother several times and also tried to look at the place that I'd fired at previously. The shooting was getting closer and closer to our home, so I looked across my shoulder several times. I looked around the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then what happened and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother disappeared. She slipped out of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you say something to her before she left the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't leave the house, rather she went back to the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do? What did you and your mother do? You left the house at some point. I want to come to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it better be made clear whether they left together or not together. The question seems to presume that, so it should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think that could be clarified very easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not yet because I haven't got to that point yet. I'm still trying to get to the point where they leave the house either together or alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will get there. We are getting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're in the house with your mother, you're looking out the door, your mother disappeared from view in the house. What happened then in the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to get her. She wanted to get a change of clothes. I told her that wasn't necessary. I told her to just grab something that was handy and we had to run because there was nothing else for us to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did your mother do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She put some footwear on. I can't remember what exactly, but she was quick and then we left the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you leave the house? Describe how you left the house.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left we didn't go far from the house itself. We went as far as a low wall near the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As -- did you leave the house together or did one of you go in front of the other. I want you to describe how you left the house and what you were doing, both of you were doing, when you left the house.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother was behind me at this point in time. We went two metres from the house, got near this low wall that I told you about, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you say anything to your mother as you were leaving the house about where you were going or what you wanted her to do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told her exactly how far she should go, where she should go to, and where we would go from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you tell her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told her to run to a house. There was a fruit tree near it. I told her to try and run across the street and that I would do my best to cover her to the extent that I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you mean by doing the best to cover her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of firing over that way. I would be returning fire while she was running across the road, so there was a chance that the firing would stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you in fact fire when your mother was leaving the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was still behind me. I didn't let her go until I cast another glance in the direction in which I was about to start firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do? You said your mother was running across the road; what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had not yet started running. There's something else that is really important that happened then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's that? What was the important thing, the really important thing, that happened then?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at the neighbour's house, Ivan Stojanovic's house. His mother was sleeping in the house that night. On her balcony there were five soldiers. Those were no HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which army were they from?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell, but I assumed they were Muslims. They carried rifles and they were looking down on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform, the sort we didn't have, the pattern was a great deal smaller and it was the colour of sand. They also wore green berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standing there on the balcony looking down into the street a bit to the right facing the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened then? What happened after you looked up and saw the five soldiers standing on the balcony of Ivan Stojanovic's house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked behind me to make sure my mother was still there, to make sure she was near me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard a woman's voice cry out, Ivan, my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you recognise the voice?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whose voice was it?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Anica Stojanovic's voice; she was the mother of Ivan Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was the voice coming from?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From outside her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you see her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked that way and I saw her half-seated. There was a soldier standing next to her. He [Realtime transcript read in error "she"] shot her in the head using an automatic rifle at point-blank range, single shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said she was half-seated. What do you mean by half-seated?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She sort of fell down, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe the soldier.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A very large man wearing a green beret. On his right-hand side a knife and -- on his left-hand side a knife, and on his right flank a gun, holding a Kalashnikov rifle. He was about 198 or 200 centimetres all, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re, in the transcript of the answer of the previous question the witness answered: "She shot her in the head using an automatic rifle at point-blank range."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We need some clarification on that "she."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I want to clarify something in the transcript. The transcript says: "There was a soldier standing next to her. She shot her in the head using an automatic rifle at point-blank range, single shot." Did you say "she shot her" or "he," the soldier, "shot her," Anica Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he then shot her in the head with a single shot using an automatic weapon, and that's a quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said it was at point-blank range. How far -- how close was he to her when he shot her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three metres maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said: "She sort of fell down, that sort of thing." Can you describe a bit more fully the position she was in before he shot her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was seated with her arm reclining backwards to keep her from falling on her back altogether. I suppose that's why the arm was slightly behind her body.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the shot kill her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He shot her in the head. She just fell down on her back, so it must have killed her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how far were you from the soldier who shot her in the head?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 15 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, was Anica Stojanovic a civilian or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she armed when the soldier shot her in the head?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she wearing a military uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothes. She was wearing a dress.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was your mother when this happened, when you saw the soldier shoot her, Mrs. Stojanovic, in the head?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind me near the door. I didn't allow her to see what was going on. I meant to protect her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened then? What did you and your mother do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I then told her it was time to go, that we can no longer afford to wait. I told her where to go exactly. This place could be seen from our door. I told her not to go anywhere out of my sight in case she wanted me to protect her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Go on. Tell us what happened then.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sort of peered to look in that direction I told her to go. There were no soldiers around. At this point there was a lot of smoke. There was a cowshed burning right behind us. I opened a burst of fire and I told her to run.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you shoot, in what direction?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told her to run to where that -- I shot in the direction where that soldier was but more into the air just for safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did your mother do? Did she run?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She ran across the street to where I told her to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started running, too, but I didn't follow her. I jumped over the fence and found myself in an abandoned garden. I realised I had to conceal myself and not keep running.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What could you see from there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a clearer view of the house and the road junction with an open area next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers that weren't HVO soldiers when you were hiding in the bushes?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Five soldiers on that same terrace in Anica Stojanovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them went up to the roof and faced the woods, and that's where the first shooting had come from that I had heard. He put his hands near his mouth and he said, Come on, Omer, it's over.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see who he was shouting to -- sorry, talking to?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I could hear was a cry of joy in the middle of the woods and some shots were fired into the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the bushes for, the garden for?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't specify. Everything happened very quickly, and it was all very sudden. It's difficult for me to be very specific about time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you leave the garden?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I tried to remain concealed. I did not want to show myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At some point did you leave it?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber about leaving it, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hid inside for a while so they wouldn't see me. I kept my head low. After a while I looked up and the soldiers were no longer around. I ran over to where I expected my mother to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ran to that place, but my mother wasn't there. She had probably run on. She must have been stunned or very scared, and she went somewhere I'd never told her to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear any voices?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got to this place where she was supposed to be, just behind that house I heard a voice saying, Stop, Grandma, we won't harm you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soon after that I heard several shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the shots relative to where the voice was?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the voice was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far was the voice?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 metres away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You heard some shots --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I can move the microphone closer to me. I'll try. It's got a very short cord on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where -- you said you heard some shots. Did you hear -- did you see a person -- did you see anyone shooting?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw no one shooting. After the shot I looked in that direction and I saw a soldier who was very old. At least I thought that he was very old.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: By "very old," what age are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a soldier, in my opinion 50 is old, and that is how old I thought he was, looking at his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform, but it was not a camouflage uniform. It was some sort of a special uniform with some sort of stripes. It was an olive-green uniform with some sort of black vertical stripes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was holding an automatic rifle in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he of the HVO or another army?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my learned friend well knows that it's not necessary to be a member of any army. He might be a member of a police unit, so the alternatives that are being put there do not form the complete set and is therefore a leading question in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that Mr. Re could put this question in another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he of the HVO or was he of another military outfit?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell at all. I couldn't see of course the emblem.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he one of yours?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw such a soldier before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do then when you saw him with the automatic rifle in his hand?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I ducked under the wall again and I waited for a couple of minutes to see whether he would leave or would set out in my direction, generally to see what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He disappeared from that spot and I ran to a wall which was near that place, which was just below the road, and there I stopped and I looked around. There was no one within my sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So a couple of minutes after that behind that house - from the direction of the house of Anica Stojanovic, in other words - a soldier came. He was quite tall, and he was wearing the same outfit as the soldier that had killed -- that had shot Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you form any impression about whether or not he was the same soldier?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had everything the same. He had a pistol and a knife. His height was the same, his outfit was the same, the cap, the rifle, the size of him was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do and what did he do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hid there, and he did not go on straight from there, but he turned left to another part of the village uphill. The name is Ratkici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it Rakic or --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Ratkici, R-a-t-k-i-c-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited for a while for him to get away, some distance -- several metres in fact, 20 or 30 metres, I'm not quite sure. And I felt that it is a chance for me to leave the spot and to try and catch up with my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah, go on.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After having covered some 50 metres, I saw my mother lying across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe how she was lying.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was lying horizontally on her stomach across the road and -- not longitudinally but across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was your reaction to seeing your mother there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not stop. I thought that she had been stopped dead. I was aware that this was not a movie and that I had to save my own life and I kept running.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you run to?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually ran across her -- over her towards the house of Anica Stojanovic, from where I could take a left turn in order to avoid the clearing -- sorry, actually I took the turn to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You ran across your mother and where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I literally jumped over my mother because she was lying in the middle of the road. And I continued straight in the direction of the house of Ante Stojanovic. There I saw him lying dead not far from his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Ante Stojanovic, was he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he is a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he armed when you saw him lying dead not far from his house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in -- what was he wearing? Was he in civilian clothes or in military clothes?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he had a shirt on, not your regular trousers but sweatsuit bottoms and thick socks, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, where did you go after seeing Mr. Stojanovic's body?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went towards the creek, towards -- in the direction of Prozor, to the right from that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you meet any people on the way?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that for a fact they were Luka Stojanovic, Mato Stojanovic, Marko Stojanovic, Lucija Ratkic, and I believe there were another two persons but I'm not quite sure. There were a number of persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, where were they and what were they doing when you met them?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were hiding a distance about a hundred metres away from Anto Stojanovic's house at a road junction to which a pedestrian path leads only. That is where they were hidden behind some trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there still shooting going on when you met them?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really. Everything was already on fire and there was smoke rising. There was some shooting that could be heard from the direction of the base where Cer is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, where did you go after that? You said you were heading in the direction of the creek. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked them whether they wanted to go along with me, that I was going to the creek because I considered that to be the only safe place at that time, and they also agreed to go with me. So we set out in the direction of the creek. I don't know how long all this lasted, but we did make it to the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the creek?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we reached the creek, we stopped for a while at some bushes and we looked in the direction of the house, or rather two houses -- where we could see two houses and some soldiers in the road. We thought that it would not be wise for us to continue along our way in that particular direction, but I told them that we had no other option or that perhaps we could wait beside the creek until night fell and see whether those were our soldiers or not because we had no other way out of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Very briefly, what happened after that? I want to move through this part of your evidence fairly quickly, if we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. We got to the creek and from there we could see several soldiers. We recognised one of them. He was Ivan Kovcalija. We called out to him to ask him who he was. Mato Stojanovic stated his name and said that I was a cousin of his and that we can get out without any fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to? Did you stay in the creek or did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went out from that place by the creek to a distance of about 100 or 150 metres away to a woods where there were other people from my village -- other soldiers from my village, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we met with them there and did nothing in particular. We waited there. We were tired. We were thirsty. We talked to each other to see who was there, who had remained up there, whether there were any other people left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Uzdol that after -- that day? Until when did you remain in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me what the time was exactly when we met with our soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just approximately. What I want to know is what time you left Uzdol that day, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all took place before 10.00. 10.00 in the morning, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you leave Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a question that I find a bit strange. I fled the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the reason why you had to leave the area of Uzdol that day?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this spot where we met the soldiers that I knew well from my own village and from other villages and where my cousin -- where I came with my cousin Stjepan Ratkic. From there we went to the house of Rade Stojanovic because I wanted to take a drink of water because I was very thirsty. Now, not far from that place some 50 metres away or so, I'm not quite sure, there was a clearing which -- where one could -- where we could hear long bursts of fire being opened, and there I was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're saying you were shot?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm saying. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you shot?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was hit in the chin and in the chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As a result of that were you evacuated from Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At approximately what time was that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long after the time when I met with the soldiers and saw my cousin, so it was some half an hour after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said earlier "it all took place before 10.00 in the morning." Are you saying you left Uzdol before 10.00 or after 10.00?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying generally from Uzdol or until I reached this safe place where the soldiers were specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were evacuated. I'm interested at the point at which you were evacuated. About what time were you evacuated from the Uzdol area after you'd been shot?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime before or around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there still shooting at the time you were evacuated?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you taken to Rumboc and then by helicopter to Split to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear or see anything that indicated to you on that morning that mortars were being used by either side?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have recognised such fire. I don't think that they were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the tank?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I would have recognised that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you say to a suggestion that the HVO were shelling their own civilians in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really would not know how to deal with this question politically. It is quite simply quite stupid to shoot at one's own. I really do not see what the purpose of that would be. I simply do not believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show the witness a portion of video clip P312. We're starting at counter 41.43, which will be shown in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just look at the screen, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you see the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop it there. Did you see the body there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we haven't got this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for this, Your Honour. I just don't know what we're looking at here. Is this the exhibit that was shown the other day because it wasn't shown in Sanction then, so I just want to be clear that we've got the same thing that the Prosecution's got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe there's just one -- some clips from the one tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Look, I mean, if it's -- if Mr. Re tells me hat it's from the same tape that was shown in court the other day, I don't mind if he uses Sanction for this limited purpose. I just want to know what it is, and then I want some help getting it on my screen because I didn't see what was shown then. I apologise for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's P312, the video exhibit number, and I'm showing a clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can you see the video there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can just play this portion. There's a body in the video at 41.41.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Just stop it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whose body was that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Stojanovic's, aka Jampura [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just look -- we're looking at 42.16, which shows the body face up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. We'll stop the clip at 43.04.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, does that show Mr. -- I'm sorry. You said you saw Mr. Stojanovic dead. Does that show him in the same position as you saw him when you went passed his body?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the first clip or the last one? I don't understand. He was lying face down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. The word "position" might be a bit ambiguous. Does it show him in the same geographical area, the same place, as where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so, I think yes, but you can see from afar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll move to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we could play clip 46.19.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you okay to look at the clip, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that body?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is Anica Stojanovic in front of her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you saw a soldier shoot her in the head. Her body is lying on her back --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Her head is downhill at 46.48 on the clip. Does that show the position her body was in after the soldier shot her in the head?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that still show her house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, I wish to show you a photograph, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit P306.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, that's a photograph, an overhead photograph of the village of Kriz. Do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to mark some things on it. I'm going to ask you to mark on this photograph the following things: Your house; Anica Stojanovic's first house, her second house, where you saw the soldier shoot Mrs. Stojanovic, and where you saw your mother. So first could you mark with a 1 your own house, your mother's house.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark with a 2 the Stojanovic house in which you saw Ivan Stojanovic at the window.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark with a 3 their second house, the Stojanovics' second house.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please mark with a 4 where you -- where the soldier was who shot Mrs. Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please mark with a 5 where it was that you found your mother lying face down and you stepped over her, thinking that she was dead.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I just use number 5 or do you want me to use some sort of a line, because I can mark the exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What I want you to do is put a 5, but I also want you to draw a line to show the direction in which you travelled to get there.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you perhaps mark that 5 a little bit larger. Could you possibly erase that 5 and just do the 5 again.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you just continue with the line where you went and hid and the direction you took down into the village -- or sorry, down towards the creek.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And it might be a little bit out of sequence, but could you please mark with a 6 the place where you were where you stood firing into the air when your mother ran away or ran across the road.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't really see in this photograph. Should I place an arrow there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: An arrow -- yeah. If you can place an arrow with a 6 underneath the arrow pointing to where the arrow goes, please do.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P347.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On -- as of the 14th of September, 1993, I want you to tell us approximately how many civilians and how many soldiers were staying in the village of Kriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And while that's being done, while the witness is answering, could I please have 0299-2310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could make a break here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'll resume until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before the break I was asking you about the number of civilians staying in Kriz in September 1994, that is the 14th of September, 19 -- sorry, 1993, civilians and soldiers. Approximately how many civilians and how many soldiers, HVO soldiers, were staying in Kriz at the time of the attack? You can't hear?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. The question was: Approximately how many civilians and how many HVO soldiers were staying in Kriz at the time of the attack on the 14th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to give you the total of both civilians and soldiers or separately as two distinct groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Separately, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 civilians and about 10 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, do you have that photograph of Kriz in front of you, which is 0299-2310? What I want you to do is I want you to mark where people were staying, and I want you to use different symbols. If you could use a dot for civilians and a cross for soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we perhaps enlarge that photo a little bit? Is it possible just so you get the houses. Now, if he marks on that and we move it, is it going to disappear, the markings?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If it's marked and then moved, it will disappear, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we possibly reduce it so the houses are in? I want the houses on the left to be in the photo. I'm trying to get a shot of the houses so that you've got the four or five houses on the left in view as well as the ones on the right. If we could do that so it's all on the same screen if that's possible. Let's try with that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, it's a dot for civilians and a cross for soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you make the dot a bit bigger.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Some soldiers were at these positions, so I'm not sure where I should place the mark for them. I can't remember exactly who was there that evening and the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't -- could you clarify what you mean by "at these positions," please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were at Borak; I don't know who exactly. The marks that I've placed, they were there for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. So some soldiers were in their positions and not staying in their houses, but you don't know who they were, but those soldiers normally stayed in the village. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how many of those were there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, five or six usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, the photo you've marked on has got five crosses and nine dots; that's a total of 14 people. And on five of the houses you've put a cross and a dot. Does that indicate that it was a mixture of a civilian and a soldier living -- or staying in the same house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But a dot does not mean one person. I've placed a dot wherever there were civilians no matter how many. Do you want me to use dots to mark the locations of each single individuals who were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are there any Xs missing for soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure about these.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, there's a number of houses in which you have not placed any Xs or dots. Does that mean there was no one living in those houses? Or does it mean you don't know?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What does it mean? The fact that you haven't put any marking on it, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that some soldiers would go to Prozor sometimes to stay with their relatives or they were at positions, those two options. Should I put two crosses wherever there were two soldiers and I'm sure about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You've marked two crosses next to a dot. Whose house was that one?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kazo and Matko Ratkic, soldiers. Kazo Ratkic was with his wife; I am positive about that. But that's all I know about it and that's why I haven't placed any further marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've finished with that. May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original of the photograph is Prosecution Exhibit P348 and the one that's marked is Prosecution Exhibit P349.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the conclusion of the evidence in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour, and I just wanted the witness to -- I think I've been too slow. I wanted the witness to mark something extra on that. Could I ask how long that will be until that's -- would it be okay if I just inquired of the Court Deputy to indicate when that will be able to be shown to the witness again. Is it 15 minutes, or half an hour?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: One minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One minute. Well, I'll come back to it because it's topical. Anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, as to the uniforms -- I've got some questions about the HVO uniforms first of all. Did your uniform have a camouflage pattern?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it somewhat more green than the -- than the Bosnian army uniform?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in -- did you join the HVO in 1991?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I'm not positive. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Did you join the HVO before the outbreak of hostilities between the Bosnian army and the HVO? In other words, when the common enemy was the -- was certain Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, I'm afraid. Can you try to be a bit more succinct, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course I will. Did the hostilities between the HVO and the Bosnian army break out effectively at Prozor in the autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you go into action against any Serbian forces in 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't fight, but I was at military positions several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And whereabouts was that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvirnjaca. Or rather Ravasnica to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in what zone of Bosnia is that position?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near Vranj mountain, in the vicinity of Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Very well. And therefore you were a soldier who was committed to the -- the goals of the HVO outside of Uzdol and in other areas. Is that correct? In other words, you were prepared to travel to fight.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the question has been phrased properly. Whenever I travelled to Ravasnica or Kupres, we were together with the Muslims at the same front line and we shared the trenches. There was no conflict between Muslims and Croats at this time; that only happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think we're agreeing furiously on this point, but that is the fact: You were prepared to travel in order to fight with the HVO alongside Muslim members of the Bosnian army. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand your question. To attack or to defend? Because these are two different questions, if you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were prepared to take part in combat activities outside of Uzdol. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was prepared to defend my home, wherever that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. And in Uzdol it came about that military positions were set up by the HVO confronting the Bosnian army, as you've indicated. And I've got some questions for you about the front -- the arrangements at the front. First of all, was there a continuous, unbroken line of trenches that made up the HVO front line in the Uzdol area in 1993, or was the situation that you had a number of fortified positions in and around the hamlets of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is at least five questions there. If you could please ask one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was there an unbroken line of trenches in Uzdol in September of 1993 making up your front line?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Incidentally, did you have any hand-grenades in your house when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never had any hand-grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And were you shooting your Kalashnikov at soldiers from the Bosnian army while wearing a tracksuit and no military uniform at all?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a tracksuit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if a witness said they saw you wearing a tracksuit and shooting at -- or shooting your gun at that time, do you say that they're completely wrong?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would never say that they're completely wrong. There may have been a situation like that, but I find that difficult to believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, what about the -- on the morning when the killings took place on the 14th of September, 1993? You were wearing a tracksuit on that morning, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's not a question of not thinking so. The question is -- I'm putting to you as a positive proposition that you were. Do you agree, do you not know, are you unsure, or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I was wearing a tracksuit, but there's no way I can be positive about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, because your mother was in a good position to see exactly what you were wearing that morning, standing right behind you as you shot the gun. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Is what correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is it correct that your mother was in a very good position to see what you were wearing that morning?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And she's a pretty honest, straightforward, sensible person, your mom, is she?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this. This is more appropriately a matter for submission rather than cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, I believe you have to be more patient with this witness. Sometimes it happens the Defence counsel might get frustrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, my frustration is a completely illegitimate basis for me to do anything frankly, but I have to ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course you're entitled to ask the questions, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it's not fair to make comments behind a witness's back in closing speeches when you're not -- when you haven't got the courage to put it to him in open court when he's here, so that's what I'm doing. And I would -- anyway, if my friend objects to that being asked, I'm not going to persist with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But in any event your position is this: You just don't know whether or not you were in uniform on the morning of the 14th of September. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm nearly certainly that I was in fact wearing a camouflage uniform on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, now, it was the rule, wasn't it, that HVO soldiers who were on leave in the village had to keep their personal weapon with them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. The weapons you signed for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what was the reason you needed to keep the weapon with you in the house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perfectly normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. But what was the reason why you had to keep the weapon with you in the house? What was the rationale for that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why wouldn't I keep the weapon in the house? And where would I have left it anyway?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Look, one of the few benefits of being counsel at this Tribunal is that you get to ask the questions. And I'm asking you why it was that you had your weapon with you and why it was that HVO soldiers took their weapons to their homes.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they wanted to be ready at all times and because the Muslim line was nearby. There was a forest near the village and you could never be safe enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And so, in short, you had the weapons there in case you were attacked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And the reason why your mother was present in the house with you was because she'd come to help you with cooking and cleaning and generally to care for you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every mother looks after her child. Isn't that logical?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, is that what your mother was doing when she came to the village of Kriz and was present on the night of the 13th and the morning of the 14th of September, looking after you, a combat soldier, by cooking and cleaning?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She would clean. Every now and then she would cook something, but there was no electricity anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, apart from the position of Borak which you've indicated, what were the other positions where there were entrenchments around the village of Uzdol? And by that I mean HVO entrenchments.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only ever at Komin, and I'm probably in no position to know about all these positions and entrenchments. I didn't go that far from my house really and there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Stojanovic, you must have known where the other ones are -- were in order to coordinate with them and not shoot at them by accident. So I ask my question again: Which other entrenchments, HVO entrenchments, were there to your awareness in the village of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village itself or around Uzdol? Uzdol did not straddle the front line. The front line ran near Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Well, you indicated to the learned Prosecutor that there were ten positions that you wanted to point out or that you're able to point out, and I want you to give names to those ten positions.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say ten. That was precisely the reason I said I didn't know all the positions. Maybe there were sometimes reasons to be in one of those positions, but they were quite far apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How far from the Borak position was the nearest neighbouring HVO position?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to specify what the distance was as the crow flies. Not very far, 400, 500 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was the name of that position?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was that to the left or to the right of your Borak position as you looked towards the Bosnian positions?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the nearest position to your left?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: HVO position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left, Gradac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how far was the Gradac position?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's really difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had Brdo between us, and it's very difficult to say what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you have a direct line of sight to those two neighbouring positions or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To which one?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was your position at Borak attacked on the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers from your village of Kriz in that position at Borak on the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Some of them were there or should have been there, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Didn't any of them tell you whether or not they'd been there at later times?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never liked to talk about it, and I started to forget it all as quickly as possible. And then later after 1994 I didn't live there, so I really cannot reply to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. In between your position and the neighbouring positions, were there any forests or trees?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And in short, were you aware of the possibility of soldiers from the Bosnian army side infiltrating through the gaps between your position and those on your left and right?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "infiltrate," you mean penetrate, pass through?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you -- sometimes did you send out patrols to cover those gaps between your front line position and your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you did that in order to make sure that soldiers from the Bosnian army didn't infiltrate up to Kriz or other villages and come near to the communications centre at Cer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because it is the fact, isn't it, that the battalion headquarters was at Cer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "headquarters," how do you mean that? Do you mean that all these soldiers should be there or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I mean that that is the battalion headquarters. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's where the tank was normally positioned. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was normally there. And as to whether it was there at all, I personally know that there was one there twice. And that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you know that there was one there on this morning, and I suggest to you that you know that because the crew of that tank were killed. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there and I cannot agree with that. I believe that is more of an answer than a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, is your position this: You don't know whether there was a tank at Cer and whether the crew of that tank were killed in the fighting that very morning. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard later that they had been killed. I didn't see it myself, and I cannot claim whether there -- there was a tank there that day because I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, okay. But in any event -- and furthermore, is it your position that you simply didn't notice any shelling in or around the area of Kriz coming from HVO artillery of various sorts when you were there on the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this question for me a bit so as to avoid its containing the answer and allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm putting to you -- let me just make it quite clear. I'm putting to you the allegation that there was in fact artillery fire from various calibres landing on Kriz and the vicinity of Kriz during the time that you were there. Now, do you agree with that allegation or do you reject it?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what's it to me that you're putting it to me as an allegation? I told you that I didn't hear about it, that I don't know about it, and what of it I really don't know. You're actually forcing me to say something which I do not know for a fact is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you're not to be compelled by me to say anything; you just say what you want to say. But I want you to look, please, at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- just excuse me one moment, please. It's Exhibit D318.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
