utterances.text: There's a document that's going to be shown to you now which is an HVO combat report which has been tendered into evidence in this court. You may or may not have seen it, but I'm going to ask you about the accuracy of what it says. Now, do you have on your screen here a combat report from the HVO with a time -- situation at 0700 hours? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you notice here that it says: "Heavy fighting is underway. Our troops are asking for reinforcement. Since we didn't have troops on the line, we sent out some of the troops that were planned to take part in the assault on the aforementioned axis." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand. If you could repeat it, and where is it exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It will be the second paragraph of text starting with "at around 0600 hours." Do you have that part?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you: Does this accord with your memory of events, what is said in the third sentence and ongoing: "Heavy fighting is underway" -- perhaps I should go back one step. "While the artillery preparation was going on the MOS launched a fierce attack on Uzdol. Heavy fighting is underway. Our troops are asking for reinforcement. Since we did not have any reserve on this part of the front line, we sent some of the troops which were planned to part on the assault on the aforementioned axis." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you know, is that accurate information that's recorded in this situation report?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this. I didn't write it. I've never seen it. This is the first time that I see it, and that is all that I can say about it, nor do I know who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you can see down at the bottom Commander Colonel Zeljko Siljeg. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw the person in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. But who was he?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You don't know who the commander was. Was he the commander of your area?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the area of Uzdol or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he the commander of the Rama Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not know that. Major Josip Prskalo was then in charge of where I was, and that is all I can say on that score.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, can you confirm that Major Prskalo was in charge of the 3rd Battalion of the Rama Brigade with his headquarters based in the school at Cer?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We're now moving to a report at 8.00, combat report from the HVO at 8.00. I'll ask you to have a look at that. Okay. Do you have that now in front of you. "Interim report situation at 0800 hours"? Do you have that in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, there's some material in the first few sentences that I'm not interested by. But I would like you to go to the passage beginning with: "Heavy fighting is underway at Uzdol." Do you have that passage? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And to your knowledge Uzdol refers to the collection of hamlets, Kriz, Zelenike, Rajici, Cer, and a couple of smaller ones. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The report goes on to say: "We are opening fire from all artillery and tank pieces. We are sending reinforcements. The MOS are at 50 metres from the school. They are encircles the hamlets of Kriz and Zelenike." Is that accurate -- that information accurate as far as you're concerned or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, at 8.00 in the morning, to your knowledge, were the HVO opening fire from all artillery and tank pieces?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. My only concern was for my own self to get out of there, and that is all that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can we go on to the next part of that order, please, which is a situation report at I think 10.00. It's the following page one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, do you have in front of you now a situation report at 1000 hours?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you read this passage here: "In the Uzdol sector, fighting is still underway. The MOS, Muslim defence forces, stormed into parts of Kriz and Zelenike hamlets. Uzdol was under a threat of becoming completely surrounded. After the introduction of fresh troops, the MOS attack subsided in strength. The command from Uzdol reported to Scipe that the Ustasha were reinforcing in the Uzdol area and that they should be hit with something. We have casualties, troops and civilians, and for the time being we do not have exact information. We have captured several MOS members. The commander of the Rama Brigade has been ordered to keep them." Do you see that passage there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Incidentally, what happened to those prisoners; do you know?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is not a question for me because I was wounded at that time. I was in the military hospital and then I was transferred to Split. I can tell you when that was; it was between 2.00 and 3.00. So I don't think that these are questions that you should be asking me. They are unnecessary, at least that is my opinion, because I have nothing whatsoever to do with that. If you want me to tell you how much time I spent in Split at the hospital there, I can also give you those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, what bears on the case here is how much time you spent in Uzdol before you were wounded. And were you still in Uzdol at 915 hours, 0915 hours?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 9.15, yes, I think so. I was still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you see this passage now -- let's keep moving. Don't worry about the captured soldiers now since you don't know about that. Do you see this part: "The situation is improving and MOS attacks are being repelled. Encirclement has been avoided. In the school where the command and CV, communications centre, were, an attack was repelled. We are still firing with artillery at the request of the sector commander in Uzdol on selected targets, Here, Kute, Scipe." Now, was that going on when you were still there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. How should I know whether they were being attacked up there or not? I only know where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But what about the hearing the gunfire of the HVO guns? Could you hear that or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a very long time ago and I cannot give you an answer to that question. I -- well, I just do not remember and that is the best answer that I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, is it the case that in the time between when you woke up and the time you were wounded, you were at all times in a very stressful and frightening situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't terrified. I didn't have all my wits about me; I was surprised. That's the best way to put it. I did know where I was and what I wanted to do and where I wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. But in terms of remembering whether you could hear the sound of artillery fire and so on, what I suggest to you - and you can agree with this or disagree - I suggest to you that you just can't remember what was happening with artillery on that morning with any accuracy. Am I right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. As far as artillery's concerned, I cannot recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I just want to now return to the structure of the -- or the situation in the village of Kriz prior to the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photo P -- sorry, Exhibit P349; that's the exhibit that he's already marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm just going to show you that document that you marked earlier on with the crosses and dots to indicate civilians and HVO members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be given some assistance here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just want you to mark -- well -- and perhaps before you mark anything, I'll just ask you the question first. You indicated to the Prosecutor that you had marked the soldiers that you were certain about. Are there other houses there where the soldiers sometimes stayed but you can't be sure they were present on the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Would you mind drawing a small circle with an open centre at -- well, I'm -- it's suggested to me that you could draw a diamond. I'm sorry about this. These documents will be tendered later. Perhaps draw a small triangle or diamond to indicate where the houses where soldiers sometimes stayed but you can't be sure whether they were present on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, do you agree that the Defence counsel ask the witness to draw on the photos which has already been admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, could I just help. I might be able to assist here. I had in mind to tender it as a separate exhibit. I think this document is already in, and if I tendered it, it would be a different exhibit altogether. And I think that would be the -- I mean, I agree with Your Honour. That's what should happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Might I inquire of the Court Deputy: Is that what's going to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Okay. Yes, I'm not allowed to write on Prosecution exhibits; I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, sorry about that, Mr. Stojanovic. Now, okay, are you able to -- are you in a position to draw a small triangle in the houses where soldiers sometimes stayed but you're not sure were there on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I just wonder if you wouldn't mind indicating the five blue marks that you've put on that document now, can you name the people, moving from left to right across the screen, who were soldiers who sometimes stayed in those houses.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just starting from the left would you say the name of the person in the furthest left house, by which I mean the HVO soldier who sometimes stayed there.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilija Kovcalija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving to the right, the next one.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Niko Ratkic, Fabijan Ratkic, Marko Stojanovic, Mijo Stojanovic. And there is another house that you cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could you draw an arrow pointing to where that house is?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. And who was it who lived in that house which is out of the picture but the arrow is drawn there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My aunt, her son, and the -- and the -- she also had another son and a daughter, but I'm not sure whether they were all there at all times. But these were the people who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you to draw a small triangle just like you have next -- on the other things next to that arrow so that later on when we look at this picture we can be sure what we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I now tender that document -- offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D350.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I have some questions about the age groups of fighters. The HVO itself, what was the age group range of soldiers on active duty in the HVO in the village of Kriz and also, secondly, in the area of Uzdol generally?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to tell you. I would have to be the registrar there in order to be able to give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Kazo Zelenika, the registrar?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I would have to be he in order to know how old these people were. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, what about an organisation called the home guard? What sort of people were in the home guard in the village of Kriz?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in charge of the home guards, and I really do not know from where the orders came that they should be in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just bearing in mind that you were a person who had been in the HVO since 1991 and that this was your home village, what was the age group of the people from Kriz who were in the home guard?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the home guards? I really don't know what kind of a duty they performed. I really don't know that there was anybody guarding me. The question is whether there were home guards, and I said that I never got any documentation or anything to that effect from anyone in the sense that those people needed to be there or had to be established there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you the question a different way. In the village of Kriz on the 14th of September, 1993, who was in the home guard?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really fail to see how I can answer your question or what is it that you are seeking with it from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just the names of the people who were in the home guard.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can answer that question. I've never seen a document to that effect, to the effect that anyone was in the home guard at all or needed to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Didn't you ask any of them, any of the older men in the village?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask about what? Whether they were these home guards?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ask any of them whether they were in the home guard or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never asked anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How long had you been in the village of Uzdol prior to the tragic events on the 14th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean how long? Wartime or generally speaking? How long I resided there for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Wartime will do.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be specific about how long. It's been a long time. There may be documents around to indicate that more accurately, but this way about a year perhaps. That's what I think at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And were there any children of school age living in the hamlets comprising Uzdol during -- on the day of the battle of Uzdol in the morning, 14th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Kazo Zelenika was there. I'm not sure if he was with all of his children, but some of his children were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, to your knowledge young kids were present in various of the hamlets. I mentioned Stjepan Zelic, Jadranka Zelenika, and Marija Zelic. Do you agree that they were all school-aged children.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrija Zelenika. I don't know anyone named that. Is that mistake perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we heard each other correctly there. The people I mentioned are Stjepan Zelic, Marija Zelic --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- and Jadranka Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jadranka was there; I'm positive about that. She's a relative of mine

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, although they were school-aged children, the school wasn't functioning but in fact was a military command post and communications centre, wasn't it, at that time?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean the school wasn't functioning. There were no classes for those kids. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. Were classes being held at the school?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in July of 1993, had the HVO leadership or the political leadership instructed civilians to leave the village and go to Prozor?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you just repeat the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 1993, July.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically whether it was then, but I am familiar with the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But whatever the date was of that order, there had been an order before the 14th of September, 1993, that civilians should leave Uzdol because of its proximity to combat -- sorry, because of its proximity to the Bosnian army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it in writing, but I did hear about it. There was an order of some sort, but I didn't see it. I didn't see the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Anyway, you've indicated what you knew, but you also knew that many of the citizens and civilians in particular had in fact left the village or the villages and gone to Prozor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Prozor, Rumboci, depending, I'm not sure. Many people did leave. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the vast majority of those who left were children, old people, and mothers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the old people stayed behind as far as I remember and most of the younger ones had been evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The kids had been evacuated?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And during your -- during September of 1993, the village of Uzdol consisting of the hamlets that were there was effectively an armed village ready for combat if attacked by the Bosnian army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "armed," what exactly do you have in mind? Speaking for myself, I only had an automatic rifle, and I'm not aware that there were any heavy weapons around in the village of Kriz. Had there been any, I would have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness just be shown Exhibit D350 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to show you that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's on the screen already. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, having a look at that photograph, do you have on the screen the photograph that you marked with the diamonds -- with the triangles, dots and houses?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Most of the houses had a soldier living there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that I've marked, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the soldiers were required at all times to be armed and to have their personal weapon and ammunition with them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each man made his own decision, depending on how safe they felt. I've never seen an order to this effect. It was a matter of common sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. You had your Kalashnikov with you because you were told you had to have your Kalashnikov with you. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who told you that --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one asked me to leave my weapon anywhere after my shift was over. No one ever told me that. It struck me as logical that I should bring it home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. But you've indicated you didn't have any hand-grenades with you, but you certainly knew about other people who had hand-grenades in their house, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please stop asking questions of this kind. I think there's more suggestion in these questions than actual questions. I never said that, and I never saw anyone from Kriz with a hand-grenade. If there were any around, then certainly it was not in the same place where I was. And if you could please stop asking questions of this nature because there are too many answers being suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if there's a proposition I put to you, you are -- you have the full right to say yes or no and to disagree. You're not obliged to agree with me, but I do ask you to respond to the questions when they're asked. Now, what I'm putting to you is whether or not you saw any hand-grenades, you knew that your comrades from the HVO who lived in the village, some of them had hand-grenades with them. Now, is that true or is that not true?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you aware of any civilians having grenades in their houses?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether the Zelics, who lived at the top end of the village of Zelenike, had any hand-grenades in their house on the morning of the 14th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you aware whether Anica Stojanovic, whose body you were shown in a photograph earlier on, had any weapons in her house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see her in possession of any sort of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want to take you to the morning of the 13th [sic] of September. On this occasion you've indicated that you were awoken and that you went outside and noticed gunfire. Now --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I was awoken by gunfire, not that someone shook me awake, meaning a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. Well, I didn't -- sorry, don't take it that way. That's not what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just correct. The transcript says the 13th. I didn't hear my learned friend say it. I think he means the 14th. Can that be corrected?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It should be the 14th so if I said it, I apologise. At that line, it's line 16, it should be the 14th, and I apologise if I have misled those producing the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Returning to the questions that I've got to ask is you gave a time that you woke up. And what I want to ask you is: What was the lighting conditions when you awoke? Was it fully light, fully daylight? Was it still dark? Or was it somewhere in between?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visibility was quite good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Are you able to comment on my question, though? Had the sun risen, for example?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. Where I come from when the sun rises it's already quite late.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, now it's the fact, isn't it, that you noticed bullets hitting your house and adjoining structures near your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And your house contained an armed HVO soldier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you yourself started firing back in the direction that you understood the shooting to be coming from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not right away. First I tried to determine whether the firing came from positions from which no one had fired before or from the usual positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had already been warned the previous day that there might well be an attack by the Bosnian army tomorrow, namely the 14th. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll put it another way. Did your leadership --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 14th --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the 12th or 13th, either of those two days, did your leadership, anyone from your leadership, tell you that there was the danger of an imminent attack from the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was it who told you that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you tell your mom, Go home. There's a danger of attack.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to tell her before to come home under no conditions. I never told her to come home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. But did you tell her to go back to -- I'm sorry. I shouldn't have used the word "home" there, and that's my fault. When you heard the news that there was likely to be an attack -- that there was a possibility of an attack the next day, did you tell your mother leave the house and go back to Prozor or wherever it was that she could find a place to stay?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I told her a day or two previously, but I can't be specific. I did tell her that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And why didn't she go?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She should know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What did she tell you about that? When you told her that she ought to go, what did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't think she told me anything specific, or at least I can't remember what exactly she said. I think she said nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's a proper time for us to take a break. Yes, and we'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Very briefly a small matter I wish to raise with this Chamber, and this is in respect of the provisional release motion filed by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The Prosecution's position is, Your Honour, that we do not object to that, and we will leave it entirely to the discretion of this Court. To is that extent, we're not going to be putting in, obviously, a written motion, if you accept our oral submission on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. I think that's the best way to proceed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That is what I wanted to bring up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information. And could we have the witness, please. [Witness stands down at break]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please sit down, Witness. Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Just before the break we were -- I was asking you about when you went outside. And when you went outside did you hear the sound of an anti-aircraft gun being fired from Konjsko hill?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Konjsko hill, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment, I'm sorry. Okay. And who had positions on Konjsko hill?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So is it your account that that was a Muslim anti-aircraft gun that was being fired from the position on Konjsko hill?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state with certainty, but it was a gun. It was something stronger than an automatic weapon or a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you've indicated already to my learned friend the conversation that you had with your mother. But you also said that you spoke -- you called out across the path or across the way to another house where Ivan Stojanovic lived, who was a boy who was aged about 15. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, about 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What did Ivan say to you during that conversation?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't think he actually said anything. He was at the window one moment and then he was just gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you see him again that morning?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, soon after that you saw five soldiers on the terrace of a nearby house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how soon, but it certainly was after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what I'm going to ask you about is questions about the death of Mrs. Anica Stojanovic, okay? And first of all I want to ask you: Did you see these five individuals that you saw before or after -- first of all, did you see them before Anica Stojanovic was shot, according to you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And when you saw them, was she in view on that first occasion?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you look away from those five and look to see where your mother was?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you looked back, did you then notice Anica Stojanovic on the ground in the position that you've already described, half lying and half sitting?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure if that was right after, but I looked back several times only briefly. It was difficult for any details to register. I had to look all around me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm concentrating on the situation of Anica Stojanovic now. Did you see her making her way to the position where she ultimately was shot, according to you, or did you just notice her there just one of your glances?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice her making her way there. I -- when I noticed her, she was already in that half sitting position, and there was one soldier next to her. I didn't notice any other soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. So of the five soldiers that you'd seen previously, there was only one left at the time when Anica was visible. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if he was one of them or if he had arrived from elsewhere. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But there was only one soldier visible. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you didn't hear that individual -- sorry, I'll take that question back. You didn't see or hear that individual firing any shots at Anica before the shot that you actually observed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how many metres away was this man? It must have been quite close, 20 metres or 30 metres. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three metres maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, my question was an absolute disaster then. What I meant was how far away from you? And I apologise for that inaccuracy. 20, 30 metres from you?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15, to the best of my recollection, give or take a metre or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't over 30 metres; that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I understand. And the gunshot sound therefore was a pretty loud and horrible sound when you heard it, is that correct, and I mean the one where Anica was shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just a shot fired by an automatic weapon, just a single shot, nothing special, fired at point-blank range.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But you didn't -- you've indicated that you didn't hear or see any shots fired by him before that. And I want to ask you just immediately after you say you saw this shooting, did you hear him or see him fire any other shots at her?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before that single shot and not after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. All right. And I think I had better confront you with this and ask you for your comment about it. If it turns out she's been shot three times, you've just got no idea when the other two shots were fired. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, the fact is that at that moment you were 15 -- you have indicated between 15 and 30 metres away. You had a loaded Kalashnikov and you still had bullets in it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what you said -- and what you said in this court is that you fired that gun up into the air. Is that the truth really?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you just shoot this man?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there to kill someone. I just wanted to save my life. If I'd fired at them, I would have been under threat by others, those that I'd seen earlier, and that was the reason I decided not to fire at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you'd already fired shots in anger that morning, hadn't you? In other words -- perhaps I should take that back, that was a saying. Not shots in anger, but you had fired shots that morning at targets, hadn't you, at the woods, for example?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the woods, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And you weren't shooting at the trees, you were shooting at the soldiers that you thought were there in the trees. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned fire in the direction from which fire was coming. I was firing at the enemy, whoever they may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if your story's true about Anica Stojanovic and what you saw, you could have been under no illusions that this large man dressed in green was the enemy. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. I object to the preamble, "if your story is true." So that is completely unnecessary. There's a proper way of cross-examining and we can do without those gratuitous comments in my respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Without that preamble your question still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if you remember the question, Witness, so I'll ask it to you again. When you saw this man, this large man shooting an innocent woman in the head, according to you, you must have thought this man was the enemy. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you must have known that there was going to be no mercy shown to you if you were caught. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And earlier on you had returned fire at the enemy that was shooting at you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, you were prepared to shoot, as you've indicated, in the air to scare the enemy away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So you didn't lie quietly as a mouse in order to avoid detection, but rather you shot the weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and after that I did lie quietly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But is that really true that you saw this large green man shoot Anica Stojanovic in cold blood dead and yet being 15 to 30 metres away you just didn't shoot him. Is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the truth. I did not shoot at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It is the truth, though, that the remaining civilians -- I put this to you as a proposition; you can agree or disagree. I'm putting to you it's the truth that many of the older people in the village had weapons even though they weren't in the regular HVO unit. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree and I don't know in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that a passage of video be played to the witness now. This comes from P312 and it is cued to a particular spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, by arrangement with the Prosecutor, they are going to play through this facility that they used today that passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at this passage and also listen to this passage. It lasts for about a minute, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It appears we have no sound. We need volume from where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think if the volume is turned up to full we might still get no sound, but let's see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we indicate we don't think it's a problem with the system; we think there is no sound on this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that will suffice for our purposes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, let me just ask you a couple of questions about that. First of all, who is the elderly gentleman in the brown jumper who is depicted in that photograph -- in that passage?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is Josip Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And where did Josip Zelenika live?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zelenike as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did Josip Zelenika appear to you in that photograph to be dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you go on, can I just indicate for the record, so that it is clear, that is at timer at 31.41, and perhaps it should be on the record which clip was actually played to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The passage, as we understands it, starts at 30.30 and goes through to 31.36. That's the passage. Now, Your Honours, could I just indicate before I go to the next set of questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There is no sound on that passage at all, and that the transcript that has been provided also reflects that. But now I would ask that the audio/visual assistants in this court please play a videotape which is prepared which -- Your Honours, this videotape as we understand it was provided by the Prosecutors to the Defence at an earlier stage in this trial. And I wonder if that could now be played. It's a minute long approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we just start there for a moment. I apologise. We might have to start this again. We don't have any picture here on the screen at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask, please, Mr. Stojanovic, do you have a picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We do now have a picture. We're going to have to start now from the start, however, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, as indicated -- stop there, please. Stop. Your Honours, we're going to have to ask for, and I apologise for doing this, an interpretation, if it's possible to be done, from the interpretation booth of what they're hearing here. There is no transcript available of this. There's one particular passage that we have a transcript about, but we'll just ask if the - and we apologise for doing this on a short-notice sort of a way - if that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, when this is played in a moment, I'm going to ask you to listen closely to what Josip says, and then at the end I'll ask you to comment about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could that now be played, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Up there in the north everything is on fire. Well, you can see I was here. I threw it here, the rifle. "Who took it away? "I don't know. "Did they enter your house? "I don't know. They didn't take anything away from the house. And the rifle was drawn here. You can look for it around here. It is 950 marks that is in there. Here is a bag. No, the money is not here. So now they have found the documents and look like they are taken out there so it can be seen. Well, there was also a coloured box with some Deutschmarks in it. "Where was your wife?" -- Sorry, the interpreter can't make out anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that's the passage that we wanted to play, so it can be stopped there, although if anyone wants to play it further, the tape's available and we can provide it and will be tendering it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you hear Josip, the elderly man depicted there, referring to a rifle?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know him to own a rifle?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the senior citizens of the area of Uzdol to own a rifle?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't recall anyone having a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ever notice Josip, the man who was depicted there, to have a rifle before?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I tender that videotape that was provided to us. Offer it for tender, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We don't object, but could it be identified. It appears to be a copy of P312 from, is that correct, from whatever it was that we played before, 30.32 to 31.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't think it's a copy of that. We think P312 is probably a copy of this. We don't know what the situation is as to what's a copy of what. What we can say is that we were provided that document that was shown there with full sound by the OTP. We want to tender it separately because it's got the full sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't object. We need some identifier, like an ERN or something. We don't know when it was provided or which one it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's say that we'll have this videotape admitted into the evidence at this stage. Then we'll check and compare with the previous one. If they're exactly the same with the picture as well as with the sound, I don't think we need to admit two similar pieces of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's -- it's undesirable to have two identical documents tendered, and I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe the Court Deputy could give it a number at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D351.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in due course the issue of the chain of custody of these -- each of the two can be clarified, of course, but it looks as if it needs to be clarified because the one we have has got sound, and it has got sound about a matter of relative importance when you come to consider what the situation in the village was and whether the civilians were armed or not. So we don't know what the situation is, and the Prosecution will probably provide an explanation for it in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have already made a ruling that it is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, thank. And anyway is your position this, Mr. Stojanovic, that as far as the older citizens in the village having guns, you never saw any and you don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that they had -- the older citizens had any arms; the soldiers did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And -- very well. I've now nearly reached the end of the cross-examination here. I'm not going to take you over everything that you were asked. I'm just going to take you now to the situation after you ran by -- you passed by your mother on the road and you thought that she was deceased. And then you went passed the body of Ante Stojanovic. I just want to ask you about the position of the body of Ante Stojanovic. How far from that body were you when you ran -- when you were escaping from Kriz down to the creek?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How far was the body from the house or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How far from the body was you when you saw it [sic]? I mean Ante Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that. Some 15 or 20 metres, I believe, but I cannot be sure. I wasn't near enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And when the Prosecution questioned you about whether the body was in geographically the same location on the film as it was when you saw it, you answered in the affirmative to that question. But as to whether the body had been moved to some degree or not, you are simply not able to comment, and I mean moved between the time when you saw it, in flight, and the time when the video was taken. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that he lay on his stomach. Whether he had been moved, I really don't know. When I saw him, he was lying face down on his stomach, and that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when you reached the creek you indicated that you met with Luka, Mato and Marko Stojanovic and Lucija Ratkic, and you mentioned two other people whose names you couldn't recall right now. I want to ask you: The two other people that you met, were they HVO soldiers or were they other people?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I made a mistake. Lucija Ratkic is the surname. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't think you made a mistake. If there's any pronunciation mistakes, you can attribute them to me without any problems. But in any event, the other two people who were there you couldn't recall them. What I'm asking you is: Were they soldiers? Were they old people? What do you say about them?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were two elderly people, an old man and an old woman, but they were not a married couple; of that I'm sure. But -- but then I'm not sure whether it was exactly at that same place where I saw these other people that I saw the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Just doing the best you can to remember now, was it your impression at the time that these two elderly civilians had fled and taken refuge at the creek with the soldiers? In other words, had they arrived there together or not?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I picked them up much before the creek, not far from the house of Ante Stojanovic, and they were all together as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So what you had was a group of mixed civilians and soldiers fleeing away from the village of Kriz. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Anyone who shot at the soldiers was likely to hit civilians. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How can he answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, he was there, that's how, and I would ask him to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It does sound rather speculative. It depends what you're shooting with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's all right. I withdraw the question. I'm going to deal with it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That group of people, of mixed soldiers and civilians who were walking down towards the creek together that you've described, how far apart were you standing from each other as you went down the hill there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were in a group together rather than in a row, in a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So a person shooting at a soldier in that group would have a good chance of hitting a civilian as well. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depending on the firearm used and how good a shot that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And as far as you recall, did the soldiers make any effort to separate the civilians out from them as they went down the hill? I mean the HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall there were no major efforts aimed at separating them. We did not try to drive them away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure what the witness said in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, because the interpreter had an area of uncertainty, would you mind repeating your answer. We're not criticising the answer, but it may be that the interpreter missed it. So would you just reply as best you can once again, please. Let me -- perhaps I can help another way. I'll read to you what the interpreter said, how the interpreter interpreted it, and you tell me if that's accurate or if there's something you want to add. I asked you the question: "Okay. And as far as you recall, did the soldiers make any effort to separate the civilians out from them as they went down the hill. I mean the HVO soldiers." And you then replied: "Well, as far as I can recall, there was no major efforts aimed at separating them. We did not try to drive them away." That's what the interpreter got. Does that reflect accurately what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite correctly. In other words, we did not force them to go away from us, nor did we ourselves try to flee from them as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience in answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, Mr. Morrissey asked you about whether someone in the HVO had told you of the danger -- sorry, had told you on either the 12th or the 13th of the danger of an imminent attack from the ABiH and you answered yes. Had you ever been told before there in similar circumstances of the danger of an imminent attack from the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what had happened on those many times? Had there in fact been an attack when you'd been warned before?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people in the village would be put in a state of alert, so to be as ready as possible for such an event.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many times did an attack follow a warning of danger of an imminent attack?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that the 14th of September, or are you referring to an earlier occasion when there was an attack?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not an actual attack, rather there was intensive fire. But at that time there was one soldier who got killed on the front line. But I do not remember the date with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to clarify, too, some of the questions in relation to what you were wearing when you were outside with your Kalashnikov firing into the air. Now, you told me when I asked you questions that you had worn your -- that you had a uniform. What -- and yesterday I think you said the uniform comprised -- it was a camouflage one. Can you just tell us what you wore on the top and what you wore on the bottom as part of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bottom were trousers. I had boots on my feet -- I did not have boots on my feet. I had some sneakers or something like that, and I had a jumper on, a sweater.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to divide this into two. What was the normal uniform and then I'll come to what you were wearing on the morning. So first, what was the normal uniform that you were issued with and wore?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a jacket, a camouflage jacket?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have a jacket generally, but I'm not sure whether I wore it on that particular day. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. What about the camouflage trousers, were they part of your uniform?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you wearing the camouflage trousers on the morning when you went out and shot into the air?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You had military boots, but you were wearing trainers when you went out. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So to clarify this: You had camouflage trousers on and a jumper or a sweater on the top. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the jumper or the sweater, can you describe it? What sort was it, a military one, a civilian one? What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was my personal sweater. It was a dark brown one and there was some other dark shades on it. It was a Dolce Vita with a turtleneck, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Morrissey, Defence counsel, asked you about where you found Ante Stojanovic's body, whether it had been moved. I just want you to have a look at Exhibit P306, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have a different zoom, please, because if it's this blown up, I cannot see it properly. I can't see every blade of grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't think the photograph's there yet. Can you see on P306, which is in front of you, the spot where you saw his body? Can you see the photograph on your left there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see the photograph, but I cannot see the actual place. It is really too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you saying that it needs to be blown up or it's not -- it's in another position, not actually on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I'm saying is I can't see the place properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About where -- was it near the village of Kriz that you found his body or saw his body?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vicinity of his house, more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see his house there?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was his house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I mark it or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, if it's not there -- I'm sorry. Can you see his house in that photograph? Then you said can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you can see it, can you mark the house, please.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where was -- you've put an X on his house. Now, where was the body in relation to that when you're saying it's over the hill? Could you perhaps put an arrow pointing down to where -- the approximate place where the body was.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not sure, but I think hereabouts, roughly speaking, or perhaps further to the left. I'm not sure what the scale is of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I'll show you from the other view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection -- there's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P352.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I trouble the registrar to show the witness Exhibit P333, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that one help? All right. Can you see the spot there where you saw his body?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark just with an X the spot where his body was.

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not positive, but if memory serves, it was around about here. Certainly not far from the spot that I've marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the X that you've put, is that in front of his house?

utterances.speaker: JANJKO STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P353.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, are there any more documents to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's nothing new, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the room, and then we wish you a very pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We still have about 30 minutes to go until 7.00, so it's possible for us to hear the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you give your full name to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Marko Zelic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And you were born on the 12th of July, 1978?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And you were born in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your current occupation is that you're a waiter?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Not as we speak. I've changed jobs recently.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What are you doing now?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I'm a construction worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, before the war, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: In Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And which part of Uzdol was this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Zelenike.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And who did you live with?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: With my mother, brother, and sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you please give their names?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Ruza Zelic, Stjepan Zelic, Marija Zelic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And can you tell us how old was Stefan [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And Marija?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And how old were you yourself? And I'll take the date of 14th September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you going to school?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: 15. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'd like to take you to the 14th of September, 1993. Do you remember that date?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us what happened on that day and start with the morning, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: That morning I was awoken by sounds of shooting near my house. We realised immediately that something was wrong and we started running.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take this a little bit slower, if I may, and I need a little bit more detail from you. What time was it in the morning that you woke up?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: It was about 6.00 a.m. thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did your other members of the family also wake up at about the same time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Right. And you said you heard some sounds. Can you describe those sounds again, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Sounds of shooting, automatic weapons being fired. We started running. We left the house and started running towards the school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And did you all have time to dress before you left the house, or did you leave in your nightclothes or whatever?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I ran in my nightclothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what about the Stefan, your brother?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: The same applied to him. He started running like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And your sister, Marija?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And how did you leave the house, through which exit?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Through the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you see any of your neighbours at that time before you ran up to the school?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: We started running towards the school building and towards our neighbour's house, which is on the way to the school. We saw that the neighbour's cowshed was burning, and we decided not to run in the direction of his house but rather to the woods. I saw my neighbour outside the house. He was unarmed and there was a soldier standing next to him who was armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what is the name of this neighbour?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Ivan Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And how long was it that you were there to observe this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Not long. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And this soldier who was standing next to him and who was armed, what soldier -- whose soldier was he?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: He wore a camouflage uniform and carried a weapon. I wasn't sure whose soldier he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Then what did you observe?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I saw my neighbourhood standing right there six or seven metres from the house itself, and I saw this soldier carrying a rifle. Once we surveyed the scene, we decided to start running in a direction through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to Ivan Zelenika before you ran away to the woods?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. There -- there were sounds of shooting all over the place all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And where did you run to? Which woods were these?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: The woods right next to our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And would the registrar please put on this. That's 0149-4763.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: There will be a photograph appearing on your monitor in a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 354.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Right. Now, could you mark for us - and you'll be assisted in a minute - with a circle where your house was.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And can you mark with an arrow the direction you ran and how far away from the house you ran.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: We ran down as far as the road junction. I managed to dive into a creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this junction, just -- on this photograph that you're still looking at, where exactly was the junction and can you mark it with an X?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And if you could also make your arrow bigger and mark with a cross this junction where you just mentioned was.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll tender this into evidence, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But I will now like to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the Court Deputy will give a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P355, and the original Prosecution Exhibit P354.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you. What I -- can I please have 0149-4712 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 356.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Is it on the screen? I can't -- oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, is this the junction that you just referred to, it's a close-up of that junction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you tell us what happened here but take it a step at a time. You were all at this junction. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I was the first who managed to escape further down from the junction and as far as the creek, but my mother and sister stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Escape from what? Can you just tell us what happened? Did you see anybody here or you just separated -- you ran somewhere else and your mother and sister and brother ran somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I was the first to escape. There was firing and I noticed soldiers running after us.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, how many soldiers did you notice running after you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of soldiers they were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: I heard them yelling "Allahu Akbar", and I assumed those were Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What kind of uniform were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you recognise that camouflage uniform as belonging to any particular group?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: No. They all looked alike, but there was nothing distinctive about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And were they saying anything to you? To you I mean by your entire family.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: They were telling us to stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And did you stop?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: No. I just ran on.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And where did you run?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
utterances.text: Further down from the junction and towards the creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Before you ran to the creek did you -- were you -- did you -- were you close by this photograph somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC
